extracted.intended_audience: preschool and primary teachers, teacher-educators, and educational researchers interested in embodied/arts-based approaches to teaching elementary mathematics
extracted.subtask_description: Designing and leading experiential sessions and teacher workshops that integrate dance, music, drawing, and literature to teach primordial geometric concepts to kindergarten and early-primary children (and to train teachers by having them enact children's activities).

rubrics_metrics.name: Integration of arts (dance, music, visual arts, picture books)
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigate the teaching and learning of mathematics through the integration of dance, music, visual arts, and picture books.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The program uses music to support and nurture dance, drawing that originates from movement, and picture books to bring words and visual arts into the experience. Arts integration is intended to make mathematics perceivable and enjoyable, and to connect imagination, mimesis and mathematical reasoning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Focus on dynamic aspects of elementary mathematics
rubrics_metrics.description: Target dynamic mathematical aspects such as iteration, ratio, motion along the number line, and the generation of lines and solids.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design activities that foreground processes and motion (e.g., how lines are generated by movement) rather than static computation; these dynamic topics are well-suited to embodied/kinesthetic exploration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exploit mimesis-somatic understanding
rubrics_metrics.description: Employ mimesis (somatic, mimetic movement) as a key cognitive resource for children’s mathematical understanding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourage participants (and teachers) to 'become' things/people-in-action to grasp mathematical ideas pre-linguistically; have teachers step into children's shoes so they experience mimetic learning first-hand.

rubrics_metrics.name: Three pedagogical pillars for session design
rubrics_metrics.description: Base sessions on: a) exploiting mimesis-somatic understanding, b) combining in-motion whole-body experience with sitting graphical work, and c) math talk on the shared lived experience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These pillars guide the balance of embodied activity, representational work (2D/3D translation), and reflective discussion to move from experience to conceptualization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Structure sessions in phased sequence with timed activities
rubrics_metrics.description: Organize the session into phases (e.g., Opening ritual, Warm-up, Blowing exercise, Tracing in the air, Graphic representation, Reading a story, Cool down, Discussion/Reflection, Diary) with explicit time allocations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The paper provides a sample schedule (20 + 40 + 20 minutes split across phases; specific minutes per activity like 5, 15, 10, etc.). Use timing to scaffold attention, exploration, and reflection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use opening ritual and warm-up to support attention and presence
rubrics_metrics.description: Begin with rituals that orient participants into the space (e.g., stepping into marked points on the floor) and short energetic warm-ups to build awareness and concentration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rituals and warm-ups (example: 'taking a shower' imagery, deep inhalation/exhalation strokes) prepare participants physically and mentally for embodied exploration and enhance their ability to enjoy the aesthetic/mathematical experience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design partner and small-group configurations deliberately
rubrics_metrics.description: Use pairs and small groups for specific exercises (e.g., pairs for blowing-on-the-body and paired drawing; two larger groups for story-movement split).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Groupings serve pedagogical functions: partners for guided tactile/kinesthetic guidance, pairs for mutual drawing interpretation, and groups to alternate listening/moving and drawing. Explicit role switches are used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Safety and gentle facilitation in partner work
rubrics_metrics.description: Partner exercises must be performed with great care and gentleness, avoiding pulling or pushing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Teachers should emphasize safe physical contact, guide exploration organically, and model appropriate touch; safety is essential for trust and effective mimetic engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use music purposefully to shape movement and signal structure
rubrics_metrics.description: Select and use music to provide rhythm and imagery for movement; associate songs with particular body-initiated movements and pause music at irregular intervals as part of the activity structure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: assign specific songs for movement starting from head/arms/legs; pause/resume music to signal marking of an imaginary point and change of direction. Music choices and timing should scaffold the kinesthetic experience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Teacher modeling and leadership role
rubrics_metrics.description: A single instructor leads the collective process, demonstrating exercises and guiding transitions between movement, drawing, and reflection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Teachers participate alongside learners during PD to experience the activities as children would; instructors must model pauses, marking points, and how to translate movement into graphic representation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Translate embodied movement into graphic/paper representation
rubrics_metrics.description: After movement, have participants recall their motions (eyes closed optionally) and create two-dimensional representations on paper of the points and straight lines they produced in the air or on the floor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide large paper (A3) and tactile art materials (wax crayons, pastels, thick markers). This step links 3D embodied experience to 2D symbolic representations, supporting conceptualization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integrate literature/storytelling to connect narrative and geometry
rubrics_metrics.description: Use picture-books (example: 'Red Line, Blue Line') read aloud while participants either move to embody protagonists or draw to visually interpret the narrative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Divide participants so one group moves while listening and another draws; story-driven activities support imaginative engagement with geometric relations (lines, interactions, colors).

rubrics_metrics.name: Include cool-down and breathing to close embodied activity
rubrics_metrics.description: Conclude movement with a cool-down (seated circle, focused breath) to create calm and allow transition to reflection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: ten slow deep breaths, collective gentle gestures (blowing fingertips, clapping) to provide closure and emotional regulation after active exploration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Facilitate guided reflection (math talk) using specific prompts
rubrics_metrics.description: Use structured questions for pairs to analyze graphic works: note observations, identify at least three geometric objects/conceptions present, and write three words summarizing the experience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collect pair responses on a large sheet divided into 'lived experience' and 'mathematical conceptions'; use these to scaffold whole-group discussion and development ideas for other age groups.

rubrics_metrics.name: Require written reflection (diary) to consolidate learning
rubrics_metrics.description: End the session with individual diary writing (e.g., 10 minutes) focusing on personal reflections, connections across arts and math, and mathematical themes that emerged.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Diary writing supports metacognition, links experience to symbolic thought, and provides material for teacher learning and documentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Target primordial geometric concepts explicitly
rubrics_metrics.description: Center activities on primitive/primordial geometric conceptions such as plane, point, (straight) line, angle, distance, parallelism, intersection, on, betweenness, and congruence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize some concepts as primitive/undefined in Euclidean axiomatics; design embodied tasks that make these primordial notions perceptible and discussible with children.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scaffold difficulty and allow extended exploration for challenging initiations
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide extra exploration time for movements that are harder to initiate (e.g., starting movement from feet and legs) and adjust pacing to ensure full engagement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Teachers should be prepared to lengthen exploration phases for certain body-initiated movements and to model strategies to help participants engage bodily.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use specific materials and spatial setup
rubrics_metrics.description: Prepare the physical space (mark points on floor with tape, arrange circle formations) and provide art materials (A3 paper, wax crayons, pastels, thick markers).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Physical marking and materials support orientation, bodily positioning, and the transition from movement to graphic representation; plan the room layout in advance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encourage adaptability and transfer to other educational levels/audiences
rubrics_metrics.description: Observe overall composition and reflect on how activities might be developed or adapted for secondary students (Grades 6–12) or adult audiences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use participants' reflections to consider extension tasks, increased abstraction, or additional mathematical rigour when adapting activities for older learners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Embed documentation and researcher immersion in program design
rubrics_metrics.description: Document learning and teaching processes and employ researcher immersion in lived experience as part of the program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Systematic documentation and researcher participation help evaluate outcomes and refine workshop design; the broader EU-funded project emphasizes this as crucial.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aim to foster mathematical reasoning, argumentation, and enjoyment
rubrics_metrics.description: Design activities trusting in children's capacity for reasoning and argumentation, making aesthetic experience a route to mathematical awareness and enjoyment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Activities should not be purely performative; they should prompt speculation, conceptual unraveling, and opportunities for children to verbalize and argue about mathematical observations.
